question: Should OpenClaw core support a first-class per-agent backup/restore/clone contract, and if so what should happen to auth profiles, session transcripts, existing agent ids, and restore-as renames?
rationale: The request changes sensitive persisted-state and recovery semantics and overlaps active backup/restore work, so automation should not choose the permanent CLI/API contract.

options.title: Design core per-agent restore
options.body: Sponsor a core design that defines archive contents, restore-as rewriting, auth/session handling, overwrite behavior, rollback, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into snapshot work
options.body: Require the active encrypted-snapshot backup work to settle whole-instance restore first and add per-agent scope there only if the same manifest contract can safely cover it.

options.title: Keep external for now
options.body: Leave per-agent cloning to documented manual or external tooling until maintainers want a built-in recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Design core per-agent restore
recommendation.body: Sponsor a core design that defines archive contents, restore-as rewriting, auth/session handling, overwrite behavior, rollback, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current backup CLI surface and own the active adjacent backup/restore PR referenced from this issue.
